assertion.statement: For the fixed maximal CM order, type, split level orientations and reduction place, reduction is an ideal-class-equivariant multiplicity-one bijection onto the labelled target component with the induced inert-prime orientation; it gives the same unaveraged finite sum lambda_M(overline(L P_D)).
assertion.objects: CM triples with labelled maximal O_F action and cyclic N subgroup; labelled supersingular triples and optimal O_F embeddings; Pic(O_F) acts on both. The target uses the pointwise centralizer F^times.
assertion.hypotheses: F is imaginary quadratic with units ±1; q=ell_0 is odd, inert and unramified in F; (N,q disc(F))=1 and every prime of N splits in F. Retain CM ideal reciprocity, good reduction and specialization, and the separate geometric/Tate-lattice description of enhanced supersingular curves with Frobenius compatibility.
assertion.quantifiers: For every ideal class, with one fixed CM type, reduction place and orientation tuple; restriction to each underlying supersingular pair preserves the bijection on its fiber.
assertion.parameter_range: Maximal order and conductor one only; arbitrary split prime-power level including powers of2, and odd inert q including3 when the stated hypotheses hold.
assertion.uniformity: Multiplicity one for each component. One fixed L, parametrization and additive lambda_M are used for the whole finite class-group sum.
assertion.constants: No division by the class-group size. The later stabilizer factor1/2 and coefficient mass are separate arguments.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same Artin action on CM points and ideal quotients. Simultaneously inverting the class labels leaves the quadratic-character sum unchanged. Keep the two q-residue orientations distinct.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The opposite q orientation is obtained by Frobenius or conjugate CM type, not as the image of the same fixed-type reduction. The map to unlabelled curves need not be injective. Extra quadratic units are excluded.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the place and actual reference CM point before reducing all classes. Prove the labelled target torsor without assuming reduction surjectivity, then use prime-to-Nq ideal representatives to prove equivariance.

assertion.objects: The one saved integer polynomial P_star, canonical codes for2E(Q(sqrt2))=Z P0, actual guarded multiplication and pole templates, and the fixed five-input natural polynomial.
assertion.hypotheses: G is exact canonical membership and addition; M is exact multiplication on every typed triple; H gives both separately used constant sets; PC supplies the specified pole witnesses; C gives natural computation and rational substitution semantics; B identifies the literal expression and its size calculation. Each requires its own proof.
assertion.quantifiers: For every q in Q, q belongs to ordinary Z iff there exist292890231904 rational witnesses with P_star(q,w)=0.
assertion.parameter_range: All rational inputs, including nonintegers; witness variables for the natural compiler are natural before its rational model translation.
assertion.uniformity: One polynomial and one set of fixed templates works for all inputs. No family-dependent replacement is permitted.
assertion.constants: Ambient count292890231905; degree strictly below tw7 and absolute coefficient strictly below tw8, with tw1=2 and right-associated towers.
assertion.normalizations: Ordinary embedded Z in Q, not merely an abstract Diophantine model; one shared shift and disjoint private witness blocks; integer coefficients.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The proof must retain identity/opposite code cases, every typed multiplication triple and its finite false-triple guard, zero/negative/nonintegral inputs, and the inverse guards in the literal construction.
assertion.limit_order: First establish G/M/H/PC/C/B for the actual templates, then apply the ordinary-value bridge and literal substitution, and finally the same-expression size bounds.

assertion.statement: For the original principally polarized QM surface A/K in the six-contact construction, one finite Galois field L contains K, defines all ordered Hom groups between its conjugates, has degree at most D and is unramified outside T; the full geometric endomorphism algebra of A is B or M2(k) for an imaginary quadratic k.
assertion.objects: The original A, W0=Res_(K/Q) A and its actual integral endomorphism lattice; the same geometric conjugates and original principal polarization.
assertion.hypotheses: The original-datum construction supplies K/Q normal of degree<=F0=324!, A/K good outside S, K unramified outside T=S union supp(M_S(u)), and common polarized geometric point; the retained published Hodge/algebraicity and good-reduction Tate inputs apply.
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational u outside the six contacts and allowed S; all conjugates and all ordered pairs of them; every prime outside T.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero, dimension A=2, dim W0=2[K:Q]; arbitrary finite rank r of End(W0), not only rank4.
assertion.uniformity: One field L simultaneously defines the full Hom collection; its bound is uniform in u once F0 is fixed.
assertion.normalizations: Full geometric endomorphisms and integral Betti lattice; action on End(W0) rather than a chosen equivariant labeling of conjugates. Betti/Tate comparison is not claimed Galois equivariant.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every residue prime is covered by choosing an auxiliary Tate prime different from it. The torsion-free mod3 kernel proof applies to arbitrary r. CM and non-CM outcomes are separated; no replacement isogenous A is substituted.
assertion.limit_order: Construct W0 and its finite Galois action first, kill that action by its mod3 kernel, then descend block Hom maps and identify full Hodge endomorphisms.

assertion.statement: For the original beta caller, alpha=det(r_5)/epsilon_5 has finite image on G_Q.
assertion.objects: The original beta caller s A over F, its polarized four-dimensional V_5(A), and the rank-two r_5 with V_5(A)=r_5|G_F direct-sum r_5|G_F.
assertion.hypotheses: A polarization is defined over the number field F, the covariant Tate polarization pairing is nondegenerate alternating and G_F-equivariant with values in Q_5(1), and the displayed Tate restriction is the actual original one.
assertion.quantifiers: Every g in the open subgroup G_F, followed by the character alpha on all of G_Q.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed original five-adic representation; characteristic-zero coefficients and finite [F:Q].
assertion.uniformity: This is a qualitative calculation for the same original caller; no controlled field is replaced.
assertion.constants: det(V_5(A))=epsilon_5^2 on G_F, alpha^2=1 there, and alpha(G_Q) is finite.
assertion.normalizations: The multiplier of the covariant Tate alternating form is epsilon_5. The determinant of the two-copy representation is det(r_5)^2.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The determinant has no unresolved sign: the square of the nondegenerate alternating form is a nonzero top form. No finiteness conclusion is inferred from a weight-zero character alone.
assertion.limit_order: Use the actual polarization pairing on G_F, compare the two-copy determinant, then use finite index to conclude alpha has finite image.

use.reason: The square of the alternating form spans the top exterior power, so its epsilon_5 multiplier gives determinant epsilon_5^2. The two-copy Tate identity yields alpha^2=1 on G_F. A finite set of coset representatives and this two-element subgroup make the full character image finite. Kato then uses this already finite alpha in delta^2=alpha/epsilon_f.

assertion.objects: The same E_l, conductor N, rational coefficient newform f, Shimura quotient q_f:J0(N) to A_f, and Q-isogeny alpha:A_f to E_l.
assertion.hypotheses: The published newform input supplies normalized integral weight-two f and its trace comparison outside 2N. Shimura supplies the rational elliptic quotient and the correspondence action. Faltings supplies the same-Q isogeny from almost-all equal Euler factors. The actual model has discriminant 2304*l^6 with l odd.
assertion.quantifiers: Every prime q not dividing N and every point x of X0(N) in the geometric neighbor correspondence.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed E_l and its actual conductor N; l is odd. No bad-prime trace assertion is imported.
assertion.uniformity: The same quotient and isogeny serve all good primes; no averaging or q-dependent rescaling is introduced.
assertion.constants: v2(Delta)=8 modulo12 implies 2 divides N; the correspondence has q+1 branches and T_q[infinity]=(q+1)[infinity].
assertion.normalizations: a_1(f)=1; pullback operator q*f(qz)+(1/q)*sum_j f((z+j)/q), coefficient a_(qn)+q*a_(n/q); the unital rational coefficient action is integer multiplication.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At level primes only the U_p eigenoperator statement is retained, not a bad-prime trace formula. a_q=0 causes no division. No Manin constant, integral homology index, Atkin-Lehner identity, local extension or reduction is asserted.
assertion.limit_order: Choose f and its quotient, compare almost-all Euler factors to obtain alpha over Q, check 2|N, identify the unaveraged good-prime correspondence, and then compose alpha q_f and subtract the fixed cusp.

assertion.statement: A bounded standard multiplier transfers small positive circle coefficients through an inverse affine substitution with offsets O(N).
assertion.objects: Real polynomial f, ftilde(m)=f(A_i+b_i m_i), integer offsets A_i, bounded nonzero integer steps b_i, product-binomial coefficients.
assertion.hypotheses: Fixed total degreeD and dimensionk; |A_i|=O(N); ftilde coefficientbeta modulo1 is O(N^-|beta|) for every positivebeta.
assertion.quantifiers: All positive output indicesalpha, with one common standard multiplier r independent of actual offset numerators andN.
assertion.parameter_range: Positive or negative bounded steps; k=1 included; no assumption A_i is standard or bounded.
assertion.uniformity: Denominators depend only onD,k,step bounds; |c_alpha,beta|=O(N^(|beta|-|alpha|)).
assertion.constants: r clears b_i^beta_i beta_i! denominators; residual error cancels the weighted coefficient growth exactly.
assertion.normalizations: Expand binom((n_i-A_i)/b_i,beta_i) over the reals; integer parts become integer coefficients afterr, then reduce modulo1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The constant coefficient contributes only to index0; it need not be controlled. A nonzero horizontal character remains nonzero after multiplying byr.
assertion.limit_order: Invert the real substitution, clear bounded denominators, separate integer and residual parts, then estimate each coefficient.

assertion.statement: The fixed real vertical character eta vanishes on every weight-m, length-R top commutator having at least two petal entries or at least one discarded (independent) petal entry.
assertion.objects: Universal U with core C, linear petals L, independent petals B; T=U_(m,R); eta:T to R; final sunflower frequency representation.
assertion.hypotheses: Full Theorem7.2 setup; final Lemma10.10 decomposition after rational-core and small-frequency removal; common fixed dimension data and standard eta; repaired additive-quadruple bias and stated independence supplied upstream.
assertion.quantifiers: Every top commutator of the specified bad type, for every allowed generator tuple; other bracketings follow by Jacobi at the top layer.
assertion.parameter_range: m=s-1, R=r_* with 1<=R<=m. The annihilation input is only on top weight m and length R.
assertion.uniformity: A single fixed eta and labelled dimension vector for the selected dense subfamily; independent of h and N.
assertion.constants: Vanishing is exact real zero, not merely zero modulo integers.
assertion.normalizations: The final decomposition has removed small and rational frequencies. The earlier pre-removal Section12 restatement is not silently used. Repeated clauses (iii),(iv) are redundant.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Bad words that already vanish impose no condition; no annihilation claim for eta on all of G* because eta is defined only on T.
assertion.limit_order: Select the fixed standard data before limit h,N; upstream proof must satisfy the all-limit conventions.

assertion.objects: Conjugate transport c(z), the orthogonal comparison j, its retained homotopy inverse, and lambda_z=PD(-,j^(-1)c(z)) on bounded free inner-limit models.
assertion.hypotheses: The actual local Kummer diagrams, perfect coefficient pairing, orthogonal local conditions/isotropy homotopies and retained duality maps are supplied. Active/moving local complexes have the displayed integral contractions in their stated localizations. The fixed old local types and old class multiplier L are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: Every finite active list and binary groupG; every allowed K split at2N; every scalar primitive constituent and height-one prime p other than(2).
assertion.parameter_range: O is the2-adic completion of Z2[[t]] localized at(2). Assertions are after the inner limit, not inversions of t in finite Artin rings.
assertion.uniformity: One fixed old-support exponent independent ofG,the active list and allowedK; actual conventions permit a=0.
assertion.constants: a=0 is permitted because z already includesL; any larger fixed nonnegativea may be retained without dividingL or changingz.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same own functional ofz, not an arbitrary dual vector. Group algebra pairing is coefficient-of-identity ofab, with permutation matrix, not normalized trace divided by|G|.

assertion.limit_order: Retain finite free diagrams and homotopies through inner limit; construct local contractions and fixed old-support comparisons; invertj in derived category and integrally on models; pair transportedz; only then compare generic values across localizations.

assertion.statement: For an abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field, rational matrix units give abelian image factors over that same field, mutually isogenous via off-diagonal units; complementary images sum by an isogeny.
assertion.objects: The original A/L with its L-defined M2(k) action, diagonal idempotents e11,e22 and a common positive integer denominator m.
assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

assertion.statement: For Q_kappa in five variables obtain the uniform nonprimitive count needed before the displayed Mobius inversion.
assertion.objects: The five-variable nondegenerate isotropic Q_kappa, kappa!=0, nonnegative smooth weight away from zero, and arbitrary nonempty sets of nonzero good-modulus quadric residues.
assertion.hypotheses: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: n=5 is permitted (n≥5, not n>5). Qκ has κ≠0, rank5 and rational isotropic point (1,0,1,0,0). Modulus squarefree, coprime to2κ, hence to2ΔQ; each residue subset is in nonzero zeros. Smooth compact support away from origin, so gradient bounded away from0. Error B^(n/2+ε)m^(n/2+ε) uniform in modulus/subsets; derivatives may depend on fixedτ. The weight is nonnegative; empty allowed sets are handled by the zero count.
assertion.uniformity: Rescale by h in Möbius sum. For (h,m)=1, h^-1Ω has same size; otherwise no contribution. Sum errors absolutely and calculate local densities.
assertion.constants: For an isotropic nondegenerate integral quadratic form F in n>=5 variables and a nonnegative smooth compactly supported weight away from the gradient-zero locus, the weighted count of all integral zeros satisfying nonempty admissible sets of local zeros that are nonzero modulo each relevant prime has the product-density main term and error O_(epsilon,F,w)(B^(n/2+epsilon) M^(n/2+epsilon)), uniformly in M and allowed subsets when M is coprime to twice the discriminant.
assertion.normalizations: BL counts all integral zeros; appendix imposes global primitivity by Möbius inversion. Hessian/determinant discriminant conventions differ only by powers of2 here. Primitive local density is1−p^-4; conditioning denominator p^4−1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Empty local sets contribute zero; n=5 is allowed. Primitive normalization is obtained by the separate Mobius sum.
assertion.limit_order: Fix kappa, the smooth nonnegative weight and tau before varying B and the admissible squarefree modulus.

assertion.hypotheses: R=κw²−xz has rank3. q is squarefree and every p|q is odd and p∤κ. Good primes preserve rank3. Euclidean successive minima; count with largest minimum>T.

assertion.hypotheses: For q<=(log X)^B and sqrtX<=Y<=X, Nm*q^2<=(log Y)^(2B+1) for sufficiently large X depending only on m,B. Mitsui applies with fixed K=E and A=2B+1, uniformly over rho,q. assertion.statement: Obtain a nonzero horizontal character obstruction for each bad one-parameter quadratic row pullback.
assertion.objects: Apply to t -> g(P(t)) Gamma on [L], with P an integer quadratic from a horizontal Gaussian-norm row. Target discrepancy epsilon=delta^kappa; dimension m and filtration degree at most 2d.
assertion.hypotheses: Q<=delta^(-kappa)=epsilon^(-1); the stretched filtration and unchanged basis are supplied by V6-GN-COORDINATES. Failure of ordinary epsilon-equidistribution gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power size and smoothness bounds. L>=sqrt(X)/B0, B0<=delta^(-5kappa).
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Q<=delta^(-kappa)=epsilon^(-1); the stretched filtration and unchanged basis are supplied by V6-GN-COORDINATES. Failure of ordinary epsilon-equidistribution gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power size and smoothness bounds. L>=sqrt(X)/B0, B0<=delta^(-5kappa).
assertion.uniformity: Internal integer coefficient extrapolation returns k*eta on the original orbit. Choose C_* first, then 6*C_*kappa<c0/2, sigma<sigma0 and 2*kappa*sigma<1/4. The internal horizontal-character obstruction contradicts total delta-equidistribution. Only ordinary distribution is deduced for each row pullback.
assertion.constants: For a one-parameter polynomial orbit on a rational filtered nilmanifold that fails ordinary epsilon-equidistribution, the quantitative Leibman theorem gives a nonzero horizontal character with epsilon-power bounds on its magnitude and binomial C-infinity smoothness norm.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Only ordinary equidistribution of the row pullback is inferred; no multiparameter theorem is used.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the stretched degree and C_* before kappa and sigma; the small exponents are chosen before X.

assertion.statement: Apply polynomial recurrence to the dense set of type-I phases d! beta_j r^j while preserving the short-arc factor.
assertion.objects: Polynomial r -> d!*beta_j*r^j modulo one on [ceil(R)] for each 1<=j<=d.
assertion.hypotheses: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.uniformity: Retain the arc-length factor in the published smoothness conclusion; the leading coefficient then has N^(-j), not merely R^(-j), accuracy. Additional factorial and product of nonzero bounded integers yield one character.
assertion.constants: If a polynomial phase takes values in a sufficiently short arc on a positive-density subset of an interval, the recurrence lemma gives a bounded nonzero integer multiple with a C-infinity bound retaining the arc-length factor and a power loss in the density.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The arc factor is needed to recover N^-j precision and cannot be discarded.
assertion.limit_order: Check that the arc is at most half the density in the large-R range; treat small R before applying recurrence.

available_assertion.normalizations: Phase values are modulo one; smoothness in the binomial C-infinity convention.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The short-arc hypothesis must be checked; no conclusion for arbitrary large arcs follows here.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix degree and density, check arc range, then invoke recurrence.

needed_assertion.hypotheses: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.

needed_assertion.uniformity: Retain the arc-length factor in the published smoothness conclusion; the leading coefficient then has N^(-j), not merely R^(-j), accuracy. Additional factorial and product of nonzero bounded integers yield one character.
needed_assertion.constants: If a polynomial phase takes values in a sufficiently short arc on a positive-density subset of an interval, the recurrence lemma gives a bounded nonzero integer multiple with a C-infinity bound retaining the arc-length factor and a power loss in the density.

assertion.statement: Factor the current polynomial orbit into smooth, equidistributed and rational-periodic factors with the stated M bounds.
assertion.objects: Initial polynomial g on G/Gamma, M0=log(2N)^max(1,C_init), external exponent A renamed B; g=epsilon*g-prime*gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: Initial basis is log(2N)^C_init-rational, hence M0-rational; fixed dimension m, degree d. Output M0<=M<=C*M0^E(B), rational subgroup G-prime and Gamma-prime=G-prime intersect Gamma.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Initial basis is log(2N)^C_init-rational, hence M0-rational; fixed dimension m, degree d. Output M0<=M<=C*M0^E(B), rational subgroup G-prime and Gamma-prime=G-prime intersect Gamma.
assertion.uniformity: epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime totally M^(-B)-equidistributed, gamma rational with coset period q<=M. B is chosen using lower M>=log(2N) before E(B) is used for the later progression threshold; no circular comparison B>E(B).
assertion.constants: The quantitative polynomial-orbit factorization theorem gives g=epsilon g-prime gamma, where epsilon is (M,N)-smooth, g-prime is totally M^(-B)-equidistributed on a rational subgroup, and gamma has rational coset period at most M, for M between M0 and a fixed power of M0 depending on the chosen B.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not require a circular inequality B>E(B); the lower logarithmic bound supplies the needed decay.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the desired equidistribution exponent B from the lower bound M>=M_0 before using the resulting E(B).

assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.

The claim is used for a general weight through separate mean/minor-arc hypotheses, not by extending the Möbius theorem.
assertion.constants: The published quantitative conjugation claim transfers a rational subgroup orbit to the conjugated quotient with the actual intersection lattice, controlling rationality, equidistribution and Lipschitz losses by fixed powers of the height bound.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. assertion.exceptional_cases: The quotient comparison is not an isometry; finite-index and Lipschitz losses and the zero-dimensional case remain explicit.
assertion.limit_order: Fix B and the resulting M, then permit fixed powers of M in the new basis, metric and equidistribution losses.

assertion.statement: Bound the first and second shifted-majorant moments in the boundary argument and obtain weighted L2 control.
assertion.objects: In a fixed enlarged ambient interval without wrap, isolate at most one constant-shift factor nu0. Set F(x)=E_m product_i nu_i(x+P_i(m)). Apply to nu0*F, nu0*F^2, nu0.
assertion.hypotheses: In F^2 use independent m and mprime; every pairwise difference of the nonconstant shifts, including across the two copies, is nonconstant. All degrees and counts are fixed, coefficients fall within A^C, and the parameter box lengths exceed the required logarithmic lower bound. The sieve exponent is chosen small enough for this enlarged moment family.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.

assertion.uniformity: The three moments give E nu0*(F-1)^2=o(1). Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz reduces any interval-strip mass to E1_I*nu0; V6-GA-GT-INTERVAL-MEAN supplies that mean.
assertion.constants: The polynomial-forms estimate for the normalized divisor-sum majorant gives the stated asymptotic for a fixed family whose pairwise shift differences are nonconstant, over the full cyclic base variable and permitted parameter boxes, with cutoff-then-size errors.

assertion.statement: Obtain the normalized majorant mean on fixed-relative-length intervals required by the boundary cutoff.
assertion.objects: Take one affine divisor-sum factor W*x+b and a fixed relative-length interval I in the enlarged ambient domain; nu0=1 is immediate if no anchor is present.
assertion.hypotheses: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain E1_I*nu0=|I|/n plus the stated iterated errors. Together with weighted L2 this gives O(epsilon)+cutoff error+size error for boundary strips.
assertion.constants: The normalized divisor-sum convex-body estimate gives the mean of a single unit-residue affine majorant over a fixed relative-length interval, with the stated iterated cutoff and size errors. This is a singleton specialization of the source estimate.
assertion.normalizations: This is a specialization of a proved divisor-sum/convex-body estimate, not a separately named interval-prime theorem. No claim that global L1 or global Gowers smallness alone implies the interval mean.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Global L1 normalization alone is insufficient; use the one-form convex-domain divisor-sum estimate.
assertion.limit_order: Freeze v and epsilon before size; only then pass to the outer cutoff limit.

assertion.hypotheses: Fixed a>=2, C1<C2<C3 and q<=A^C1, n*A^-C3<=J<=n*A^-C2. For p not dividing W*q the cube gradients give 1+O_a(p^-2). For p>v dividing q use 1+O_a(p^-1); log q=O(v) gives O(v/log v) such primes.

assertion.limit_order: Subgroups and quotients are constructed once before any sequence of polynomial maps.

assertion.statement: Basic group commutators give integer normal forms in free nilpotent groups, and their fixed-length classes form a free abelian lower-central basis. This yields integral Hall coordinates, lattices, and exact lattice intersections for the upward-closed monomial quotients used here.
assertion.objects: Free nilpotent group of class m, associated graded Lie ring, free real Lie algebra, finite Hall list, discrete group Lambda generated by exp letters.
assertion.hypotheses: Finite ordered alphabet; nilpotency class at most m. Uniqueness and graded independence are used only for the free group. Additional relations are exactly sums of upward-closed individual-letter multidegrees.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such quotient and every further upward-closed homogeneous subgroup S.
assertion.parameter_range: All integer exponents, all real coordinate parameters, all permitted finite alphabet sizes, including zero survivors.
assertion.uniformity: Coordinate maps, lattices and fundamental sets depend only on the fixed Hall list and the forbidden multidegrees.
assertion.constants: The coordinate inverse is a finite triangular polynomial; compact representatives use [0,1]^v. No unspecified finite computation is used.
assertion.normalizations: Tointon weight is bracket length; manuscript weight w is a separate positive grading. The ordered group-commutator coordinate need not be a single homogeneous Lie word.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Discarded Hall factors vanish including their BCH corrections. Saturation is proved for these monomial ideals, not asserted for arbitrary rational quotients.
assertion.limit_order: Integral coordinate proof is over standard real groups before any ultrapower.

use.reason: The actual bad-word ideal is upward closed at every weight. Apply the integral Hall-coordinate lemma to this monomial quotient, then use the separately supplied real annihilation for the character. Lattice saturation does not itself prove real character vanishing.

assertion.hypotheses: One variable, fixed degree, nonzero bounded integer b, |A|=O(N), transformed positive degree-j coefficient O(N^-j) modulo integers.

assertion.parameter_range: k=1 in the general MF-AFFINE lemma; dense progression length comparable to N in DF002.
assertion.uniformity: Denominator depends on fixed degree and bounded step, not the offset or integer parts of coefficients.
assertion.constants: Inverse coefficient from degree j to positive degree i is O(N^(j-i)); residual O(N^-j) therefore gives O(N^-i).
assertion.normalizations: Clear the common rational denominator before reducing modulo integers; no bound is required for degree zero.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Negative nonzero b is allowed; multiplying the nonzero horizontal character by a positive standard integer preserves nonzeroness.
assertion.limit_order: Fix geometry, degree and progression step bound; choose the standard denominator multiplier; transfer all positive estimates simultaneously.

preliminary_derivation.argument: If A were geometrically simple, its division endomorphism algebra acts faithfully on H1 of dimension4 and its dimension divides4. Containing B forces equality with B, which lacks a commutative semisimple subalgebra of dimension4 required by CM type. Distinct elliptic factors give a product of commutative fields, incompatible with B. A non-CM repeated factor gives M2(Q), which cannot be isomorphic to division B.

assertion.statement: For the actual non-CM conjugate D210 fiber surfaces A and A_sigma, the normalizer action gives a geometric isogeny; the full geometric endomorphism algebra is B. assertion.objects: Actual conjugate fiber surfaces of the entire principal-level-three curve, their rank-one left-B rational Hodge objects, geometric Hom lattices, and the prescribed two embeddings of F.
assertion.hypotheses: The full PEL/normalizer comparison and same-L Hom descent are supplied. A is non-CM. The rational Hodge equivalence and Skolem-Noether for the simple subalgebra embeddings are retained at their actual scopes.
assertion.quantifiers: Each conjugate surface in the same normalizer orbit and each pair of the prescribed embeddings of F.
assertion.parameter_range: Dimension-two quaternionic surfaces with B the rational division algebra of discriminant210.
assertion.uniformity: One and the same L defines all resulting geometric homomorphisms; no new field-degree cost.
assertion.constants: No quantitative isogeny-degree estimate or coherent cocycle bound is asserted.
assertion.normalizations: A finite-adelic move changes only a commensurable integral lattice in the same rational Hodge object. Use torsion density and invariant graph descent to obtain the geometric map, then clear rational Hom denominators after inner conjugation.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The F-linear isogenies need not be chosen coherently. This does not construct the later B-linear scalar-normalizer maps, sign splitting, compatible family, or bounded descent to a rational GL2-type variety.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the complex isogeny by finite torsion quotient; descend its graph geometrically; identify End^0=B in the non-CM case; apply Skolem-Noether, clear denominators and use the already fixed Hom field L.

assertion.statement: The same-field maximal-order CM factor Eprime has original stable height equal to the average of -log(2pi)-2log|eta(tau)|-(1/2)log Im(tau) after a good-reduction extension.
assertion.objects: The actual Eprime/L from the maximal-order quotient, with fundamental discriminant Delta_F; its individual complex embeddings.
assertion.hypotheses: Eprime is a CM elliptic curve, hence potentially everywhere good; the analytic discriminant formula applies to each embedding and the finite discriminant term vanishes on the good-reduction extension.
assertion.quantifiers: Every embedding of a field where Eprime has everywhere good reduction; average with division by its absolute degree.
assertion.parameter_range: CM elliptic curves over number fields, with reduced imaginary-quadratic periods.
assertion.uniformity: Stable height is unchanged by the auxiliary good-reduction extension, whose degree never enters the later isogeny bound.
assertion.constants: Analytic discriminant (2pi)^12 eta(tau)^24; sqrt(3)/2<=Im(tau)<=sqrt(|Delta_F|)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Original stable Faltings metric; individual-embedding equation6.2, not the class-average Proposition6.1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No Weierstrass-coefficient condition over Q(j) is imported from Proposition6.1; the auxiliary good-reduction field is not the isogeny field L.
assertion.limit_order: Construct Eprime over L, pass to a good-reduction extension only to evaluate stable height, apply the individual formula, and return to the same L for the isogeny estimate.

assertion.statement: For the retained global, primitive and derivative Selmer models, finite detecting evaluations give an H1 injection preserved by coefficient extension; their bounded outer quotient is a characteristic-zero DVR with uniformizer2, carrying the retained duality maps and approximate cycles as actual crossed homomorphisms.
assertion.objects: Actual retained cochain maps, product Galois groups, bounded finite detecting lists, primitive/derivative local conditions and O_infinity formed from valuation-bounded ring instances.
assertion.hypotheses: Fixed bounded minimal-model ranks, omega(k_j)≤A and a fixed number of derivative labels; retained evaluations and compatibility homotopies. Direct Selmer evaluation requires residual H0 isomorphism and H1 injection for the local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every indicated coefficient extension and each sequence of the bounded ring instances; evaluation at arbitrary sequences of group elements.
assertion.parameter_range: Primitive and derivative models with the stated local conditions. Orthogonal zero/full models only after an actual contraction at the chosen test ring.
assertion.uniformity: Detecting lists have bounded length at most dimV+dimW, selected and padded before the common limit. No support-uniform rank beyond the stipulated bound.
assertion.constants: Uniformizer2; no quantitative rank bound is added beyond the retained (5.1) bound.
assertion.normalizations: O_infinity is the ultraproduct quotient by sequences whose 2-adic valuation tends to infinity. Cochain evaluation uses the same ultrafilter, full compatibility homotopies and integral minimal-model inverses.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No continuity claim on one original Galois group and no completeness claim for the outer DVR. assertion.limit_order: Choose finite detecting lists and cone cancellations before the common inner limit; form the bounded outer quotient; pass actual matrices and homotopies; only then regard differential-tending-to-zero sequences as crossed homomorphisms.

assertion.statement: On the stated characteristic-zero nonquadratic tests, restriction to the exact common kernel is injective and two independent evaluated classes admit one rank-two localization. Finite-stage Chebotarev realizes it with exact inner-limit basis-cochain matrix equality before minimal-model denominators.
assertion.objects: The exact kernel on the full Tate module, all retained ring-class and quadratic fields; two evaluated cohomology classes; their finite localizations and original cochain basis matrices.
assertion.hypotheses: The fixed nontrivial scalar element survives the characteristic-zero test; actual evaluation is injective. The fixed matrix-span witness gives absolutely irreducible rank-two summands; moving scalar character is nonquadratic and conjugation exchanges summands. Finite quotient cochain data and finite Chebotarev are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For each such pair of independent classes and the specified finite-stage data, there is an actual kernel element and a compatible finite-stage prime/place.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero inner or outer fraction-field tests with nonquadratic moving character. Residual characteristic2 assertions are expressly weaker.
assertion.uniformity: The same inner ultrafilter gives exact matrix equality for each retained outer instance before its possibly varying denominators.
assertion.constants: No uniform denominator bound is assumed; only the existing bounded cohomology/detecting-list inputs are used.
assertion.normalizations: Kernel restriction uses the central scalar modulo the kernel, not an element inside it. Equality L_j=E_(sigma_j squared) is between original Lambda matrices before composition with I_j.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No residual irreducibility or residual rank-two localization is asserted. Quadratic height-one specializations require their separate proof. Chebotarev is used on actual finite composita, never on the product group. Long t-jets are not 2-adic approximations where t is a unit.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain the kernel element on the characteristic-zero test; place all original cochain/Tate/field data in one compatible finite compositum; choose prime and place; pass to exact inner matrix identity; only then apply minimal-model maps.

assertion.limit_order: Establish multiplication independently of Nat, type roots, apply square/addition contracts, then invoke Lagrange for completeness.

assertion.statement: The actual primitive class-functional coordinate is regular at every height-one prime of Lambda other than(2), including(t) and(t+2), hence belongs to Lambda[1/2]. This regularity also holds at the unknown full-corank-one base.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive scalar Selmer complex, its actual class and own paired functional, and the integral derivative-switch complexes over each height-one DVR.
assertion.hypotheses: The starting generic kernel has rank one unless the actual class is zero; evaluation injection, characteristic-zero detection, exact local duality and actual-class determinant switch identities are supplied. Primitive integrality holds for the old local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every height-one prime different from(2), and each finite derivative list produced by the argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Known simple-zero ring instances and the unknown full-corank-one base, with the latter used only for regularity.
assertion.uniformity: No uniform numerical valuation bound at the unknown base is asserted. Finite switch termination is pointwise for the height-one test.
assertion.constants: All switch determinant factors are units; no new numerical constant or inverse localization value is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: At quadratic specialization the two signs are defined by actual conjugation, not a ring substitution. Finite and singular planes carry opposite J actions and exact symmetric hyperbolic cross pairing. Retain D0, strict torsion factors and the actual class-functional product.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At(t) and(t+2) use sign splitting and one-or-two-step descent, not nonquadratic irreducibility. Isotropy alone does not prove U=U-perp. Primitive vectors select primes but never replace the actual class. No inverse at an unused relaxed prime.
assertion.limit_order: Localize at a height-one prime; choose a primitive generic-kernel vector for detection; use actual derivative switches until dimension one; show the actual class and own functional integral there; transport unit-valued determinant comparisons back; intersect all height-one localizations.

assertion.statement: At an actual derivative prime with nonzero finite localization of the rank-one generic actual class, switching from finite to singular condition produces a generic kernel spanned by its actual derivative and preserves the valuation of the class-functional determinant coordinate.
assertion.objects: The actual split derivative local model D0 plus(F plus S)[−1] plus D2[−2], its retained pairing, and the strict/relaxed/finite/singular Selmer cone complexes.
assertion.hypotheses: The old actual class spans generic H1 and localizes to nonzero v; its actual derivative has finite coordinate0 and singular coordinateJv. Retained integral local pairings/isotropy homotopies and exact global duality/localization identities are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: At each new inert derivative prime in the finite sequence, over the stated fraction or test field.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite and singular planes of rank2; localization v may be divisible in the integral lattice.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison preserves valuation at every allowed switch, without requiring a uniform divisibility bound on v.
assertion.constants: The common strict determinant factor, including all strict torsion, is retained on both sides; exterior-volume changes are units.
assertion.normalizations: Every condition retains D0; relaxed means D0 plus(F plus S)[−1], not the full local complex. Cross pairing is epsilon times <x,Jy>. Fractional complements are chosen to have unit exterior volume.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not require the complement of a divisible v to be integral. Exact annihilator follows from duality/localization, not isotropy alone. The derivative must be the actual class, not a substituted primitive vector.
assertion.limit_order: Retain the integral local model and triangles; pass to the specified test field; identify strict H1 and the relaxed annihilator; use the actual derivative; compare determinant lines with their common strict factor.

assertion.statement: For known simple-zero ring instances with fixed E,pi,old local types and omega(k)≤A, the actual primitive class-functional coordinate has v2 at least−C(E,A), independently of the active support and companion field.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive coordinates and bounded minimal two-term models, their primitive generic-kernel vectors, the outer DVR and derivative-switch sequence.
assertion.hypotheses: Nonzero actual central class with bounded nonzero calibration multiplier gives generic rank1; bounded residual models and outer evaluation are supplied. Nonquadratic outer rank-two detection, exact annihilator duality and actual-class determinant switch preservation hold. The paired functional has fixed denominator exponent a.
assertion.quantifiers: Every known simple-zero ring instance under the stated fixed data and companion-prime count bound.
assertion.parameter_range: Outer contradiction sequence with omega(k_j)≤A; each construction uses only finitely many switches.
assertion.uniformity: C depends on E,A and the fixed old data, not active support or varying companion field. No bound uniform in arbitrarily many switches is used.
assertion.constants: At terminal outer rank1 a nonzero minor has one finite valuation b on an outer-large set and gives v2(u_j)≥−a−b; this contradicts a sequence tending to−infinity.
assertion.normalizations: Primitive vectors select localizations; the actual inner classes and their own paired functionals determine the preserved coordinates. Terminal formula is ±alpha beta/Delta with alpha integral and v2(beta)≥−a.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No uniform numerical bound at the unknown full-corank-one base. Bounded matrix size alone is insufficient; the proof uses nonzero class, detection and determinant-preserving switches.
assertion.limit_order: Assume a countersequence; fix bounded model size on an outer-large set; reduce outer kernel dimension by finite switches while preserving inner valuations; choose a nonzero terminal minor and contradict unbounded negative valuation.

assertion.statement: For B nonzero, rational solubility of the exact pole polynomial excludes a negative odd valuation of B at every prime outside{2,3,5,7,13}.
assertion.objects: The eleven-witness polynomial Qpole, Boolean bits, signed divisor m of2730, A=mB, H=A(A−B²), and the two elliptic-curve points supplied by its equations.
assertion.hypotheses: B is nonzero and all defining equations of Qpole hold overQ; p lies outside the fixed exceptional set.
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational solution and every prime outside the fixed exceptional set.
assertion.parameter_range: One-sided obstruction only; no small-positive or denominator-square condition is used here.
assertion.uniformity: Uniform for all witnesses and all such primes.
assertion.constants: Exceptional set{2,3,5,7,13}; signed divisors of2730.
assertion.normalizations: Both point abscissas are in the squareclass A. Square scaling of the chosen even-valuation parameter preserves oddness of the abscissa valuation.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion at B=0 or at exceptional primes. This does not prove pole completeness or any converse.
assertion.limit_order: Use the Boolean and inverse equations to obtain actual nondegenerate points; assume an odd negative valuation ofB; compute valuations ofA,H; scale the even-valuation curve parameter to a unit and contradict squareness of its cubic.

assertion.statement: For an elliptic curve overQ with full rational2-torsion, two-Selmer dimension3 implies full2-infinity Selmer corank1 without assuming finite Sha.
assertion.objects: The finite Kummer sequence, rankr, cofinitely generated Sha[2-infinity]=(Q2/Z2)^t plus finite F and its canonical principal-polarization pairing.
assertion.hypotheses: Full rational2-torsion and dimF2 Sel2=3; finite-generation/Kummer structure and the alternating nondegenerate Cassels–Tate pairing on the finite quotient by the maximal divisible subgroup are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve overQ meeting these hypotheses.
assertion.parameter_range: Full2-primary Selmer corank, not Mordell–Weil rank alone.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or uniform finiteness assumption.
assertion.constants: r+dim Sha[2]=1; dimF[2] is even; hence F=0 and r+t=1.
assertion.normalizations: The divisible subgroup is the actual maximal divisible subgroup because every divisible subgroup maps trivially to finiteF. Pair finite primary cyclic factors, not the restricted pairing onF[2].
assertion.exceptional_cases: Sha may have a nonzero divisible part. The pairing onF[2] need not be nondegenerate and is not used. Pairing source validation remains separate.
assertion.limit_order: Apply finite Kummer dimensions; decompose the cofinitely generated2-primary group; use alternation on its finite quotient to forceF=0; apply the full Kummer sequence for corank.

assertion.statement: The covariant rational Hodge equivalence identifies the full rational Hodge endomorphisms of the actual complex surface with its full complex algebraic endomorphisms; with the separately supplied centralizer calculation and geometric descent this yields End^0_Qbar(A)=B in the non-CM branch.
assertion.objects: The actual D210 surface A, its covariant H1(A(C),Q), rank-one left B action and right complex structure J; likewise its conjugate A_sigma.
assertion.hypotheses: A is a complex abelian surface with polarizable weight-minus-one homology. The rank-one B centralizer calculation, the non-CM choice K0=Q, and descent of complex homomorphisms to Qbar are separate retained inputs.
assertion.quantifiers: For each actual surface and every rational Hodge endomorphism; all endomorphisms, not just those preserving the chosen polarization.
assertion.parameter_range: Complex abelian varieties up to isogeny, Hodge types (-1,0),(0,-1); the current application is the non-CM D210 surface.
assertion.uniformity: No varying-field or effective uniform bound is supplied.
assertion.constants: No degree, conductor or height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Covariant H1 and Hom tensored with Q; a polarization is an existence condition on objects, not a restriction to polarization-preserving morphisms.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The imaginary-quadratic centralizer is the CM branch and is excluded here. Hodge equivalence alone supplies neither Qbar descent nor End=B without the centralizer calculation.
assertion.limit_order: First compute the rational Hodge centralizer, select the non-CM branch, then use algebraicity and the separate geometric descent.

assertion.statement: For the two specified embeddings i,j of the same quadratic field F into B, inner conjugation gives b in B^times with j(x)=b^-1 i(x)b for every x in F; applied to j=f^-1 i_sigma f, the quasi-isogeny f b^-1 intertwines the specified F actions.
assertion.objects: The quaternion algebra B/Q=End^0_Qbar(A), abstract quadratic F and specified embeddings i:F→B and j=f^-1 i_sigma f:F→B.
assertion.hypotheses: B is the full non-CM endomorphism algebra; f:A→A_sigma is an independently supplied geometric quasi-isogeny, and i,i_sigma are the actual specified actions. The induced map i(x)→j(x) is a Q-algebra isomorphism of quadratic subfields.
assertion.quantifiers: For these embeddings there exists an invertible b implementing their specified field identification on every x.
assertion.parameter_range: Quadratic subfields of the characteristic-zero quaternion algebra B/Q.
assertion.uniformity: Existence for each pair only; no uniform degree or coherent choices in sigma.
assertion.constants: No quantitative bound is supplied.
assertion.normalizations: j=b^-1 i b and g=f b^-1; quasi-homomorphisms are rationalized Hom. Positive integer denominator clearing is a separate elementary step.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An unspecified conjugacy of unlabelled subfields is insufficient. b need not be integral. The official erratum corrects unit-group notation after separable extension; no inseparable case or deleted optional splitting-field parenthesis is used.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain f and full End=B first; conjugate the specified embeddings, then clear denominators. Same-L descent, compatibility, cocycles, Q-descent and quantitative bounds are separate.

historical_source_navigation.title: Finite Chebotarev realizations
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Milne CFT v4.03, VIII Theorem 7.4 p.259; V.1 and V.1.9 pp.152-153; finite-field application register and compatibility checks in closure-batch-008
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. Each prescribed element is the restriction of an actual Galois element, and each non-class-function use selects a place realizing that representative.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: The explicit composita, maps and nonempty classes for every registered use are given in batch 8. Existing Hilbert-class, open-image, Kummer, kernel-detection and coefficient/local-representation inputs are retained as dependencies. In particular this does not close A032, A064, A068, A070 or A080.

historical_source_navigation.title: Good reduction and finite endomorphism descent
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Part I Theorem 12.1(a), p. 55; Theorem 10.15, p. 49; Proposition 10.20, p. 50; Lemma 14.5, p. 63; Part IV Theorem 3.5, pp. 141-142 and Lemma 3.9, p. 143.
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: W0=Res_K/Q A, geometric End lattice rank≤16F0²; Galois kernel E; L=EK.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consumes the earlier finite-etale cover and good reduction construction and the restriction-of-scalars abelian variety W0.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Unramified versus good reduction: prime-to-residue coefficient prime; action on ordered conjugacy Hom comes via End(W0), not arbitrary labels.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Milne I.10.15 bounds integral endomorphism rank; a finite basis descends over a finite extension. A finite-order integral action congruent to identity mod 3 has eigenvalues 1 by I.14.5 and is semisimple in characteristic zero, so reduction modulo 3 is faithful. NOS and unramified induction show inertia acts trivially on Tate and hence End away from T. Passing to EK fixes the factor labels and all ordered Hom groups.

historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Conductor1 and ramified determinant rule out special/supercuspidal cases; obtain one unramified and one ramified line. Integral trace identity follows from diagonal matrices without dividing by2 or using integral eigenspace projectors.

historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. Each prescribed element is the restriction of an actual Galois element, and each non-class-function use selects a place realizing that representative.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.

historical_source_navigation.title: Carayol local correspondence and U_p
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Carayol sections 0.3-0.7, Theorem A pp.409-411; Casselman Theorem 1 pp.302-306, corollary p.306, Theorem 4 p.313
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Weight-two constituents obtained by multiplying weight3/2 form by theta; odd p with new level exponent1 and primitive ramified quadratic character.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: F=Q has odd degree, so no extra finite discrete-series place. All cusp eigenconstituents, old multiplicities and Eisenstein terms handled. Coefficient place lies over2; local residue p is odd.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Carayol uses geometric Frobenius and contragredient local parameter. Dualize representation AND change Frobenius to obtain X²-T_q X+q<q>. Bad Fourier U_p equals unramified-line eigenvalue only via local newvector normalization.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Conductor1 and ramified determinant rule out special/supercuspidal cases; obtain one unramified and one ramified line. Integral trace identity follows from diagonal matrices without dividing by2 or using integral eigenspace projectors.

historical_source_navigation.title: Finite Chebotarev realizations
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Milne CFT v4.03, VIII Theorem 7.4 p.259; V.1 and V.1.9 pp.152-153; finite-field application register and compatibility checks in closure-batch-008
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite normal closures of: the Hilbert class field; the moving-character radical/cyclotomic/Tate compositum; the fixed witness division torsor; finite quotients for the original basis cochains; and joint finite reductions of weight-two constituent representations. Each prescribed element is the restriction of an actual Galois element, and each non-class-function use selects a place realizing that representative.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: The moving radical multipliers respect every Kummer relation; Tate adjustment lies in the actual radical-fixing kernel. The witness detector uses one h*tau before precision varies. Finite cochains factor through finite quotients, made normal over Q before applying density. Joint representation reductions and actual elements make trace prescriptions compatible. Each extension is finite Galois and the conjugacy class nonempty; exclusions are finite.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^N(p). A rational prime supplies a conjugacy class; the chosen place fixes its representative and transported coordinates. Cochain equality is established at increasing finite precision before multiplying by localized minimal-model inclusions. No infinite-level density assertion or independent constituent prescriptions.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: The explicit composita, maps and nonempty classes for every registered use are given in batch 8. Existing Hilbert-class, open-image, Kummer, kernel-detection and coefficient/local-representation inputs are retained as dependencies. In particular this does not close A032, A064, A068, A070 or A080.

historical_source_navigation.title: Compactness, ultrafilter and finite intersection
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

historical_source_navigation.title: Dirichlet primes in progressions
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: Finite prescribed unit residue classes modulo fixed modulus; choose distinct primes avoiding finite support.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Residue coprime to modulus; all Legendre/real/dyadic prescriptions first reconciled via reciprocity and CRT. Each application fixes finitely many constraints before choosing prime.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: Signed prime parameters versus positive prime absolute values; source theorem supplies positive primes in unit classes.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: CRT gives one admissible class; infinitely many primes permit exclusions and distinctness. Does not imply a nonabelian Chebotarev condition or uniform quantitative bound.

historical_source_navigation.title: Compactness, ultrafilter and finite intersection
historical_source_navigation.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
historical_source_navigation.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

historical_source_navigation.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.
historical_source_navigation.hypotheses_and_discharge: Consume the actual quadratic coefficient factorization, fresh ramification of K, fixed nonempty seeds and detector stages with ell_0=-1 mod 2^M. Fresh ramification proves disjointness; the determinant congruence makes finite prime exclusions cofinite. Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
historical_source_navigation.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.

assertion.statement: For the actual elliptic curve E/Q, the Cassels–Tate pairing induces a nondegenerate alternating pairing on the quotient of Sha(E) by its maximal divisible subgroup, hence on its finite2-primary quotient F in the supplied decomposition.
assertion.objects: The canonical principal polarization on E, Sha(E), its maximal divisible subgroup, and F=Sha(E)[2∞]/Sha(E)[2∞]_div.
assertion.hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve over Q. The supplied finite-Selmer/cofinite-generation input gives Sha(E)[2∞]=(Q2/Z2)^t⊕F with F finite. No finiteness of the full Sha group is assumed.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve E/Q; the finite-quotient application holds for its actual2-primary decomposition.
assertion.parameter_range: Canonical genus-one principal polarization;2-primary quotient by maximal divisibility, not the unrestricted pairing on2-torsion.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or uniform finiteness statement.
assertion.constants: The quotient has paired finite primary cyclic factors; in particular dim_F2 F[2] is even.
assertion.normalizations: Cor4 gives c via Pic^(g−1); at g=1 the trivial degree-zero class makes c=0. Cor7 gives alternation. Nondegeneracy is after maximal-divisible quotient. Different primary torsion components are orthogonal.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not equate infinitely divisible elements with the maximal divisible subgroup in an arbitrary group. Current decomposition proves maximality directly. Do not infer nondegeneracy of the restriction to F[2], or finiteSha, or Mordell–Weil rank1 before RC.
assertion.limit_order: First use the separately supplied decomposition and identify its maximal divisible subgroup. Then restrict the quotient pairing to the finite2-primary part and apply the paired-factor argument; only afterward combine with Kummer dimensions.

use.reason: First use the separately supplied decomposition and identify its maximal divisible subgroup. Then restrict the quotient pairing to the finite2-primary part and apply the paired-factor argument; only afterward combine with Kummer dimensions.

assertion.statement: For the actual rational homomorphism rho:U->G, one positive integer D can be chosen so that rho(exp(D L0)) is contained in Gamma, while remaining divisible by the integer already required for BCH closure.
assertion.objects: The fixed simply connected nilpotent U and G, rational homomorphism rho, homogeneous rational basis of Lie(U), its integer span L0, and a rational Malcev basis of G adapted to Gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: The preceding construction supplies rational rho and the stated rational bases. BCH closure and cocompactness of exp(D L0) are supplied separately by the displayed local proof.
assertion.quantifiers: Every x in L0 for one D chosen from the finitely many coordinate polynomials of this fixed construction.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed finite-dimensional nilpotent groups and fixed rational bases; no varying-family denominator estimate.
assertion.uniformity: The same D works for all integer coordinate vectors x in L0 within this fixed construction.
assertion.constants: D is a common positive multiple of coordinate-polynomial denominators and the prior BCH denominator requirement.
assertion.normalizations: Second-kind Malcev coordinates identify Gamma exactly with integer vectors; rho(exp x)=exp(d rho(x)).
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every coordinate polynomial has zero constant term because rho maps identity to identity. Thus scaling variables by D clears denominators in every nonzero-degree monomial; no assertion that an arbitrary polynomial with nonintegral constant can be so scaled.
assertion.limit_order: Fix rho and bases; write the finite rational coordinate polynomials; choose one common multiple D; then evaluate on every integer vector. Increasing D preserves denominator divisibility.

assertion.statement: For every B in the stated pole-completeness domain, one common positive signed divisor m of2730 gives A=mB,H=A(A-B^2), with positive squarefree classes beta congruent17 mod24 and theta congruent1 mod24. There exist positive squarefree n,n theta congruent11 mod12 for which the full multiplication-by-two Selmer groups have dimension3 and contain the same extra class(beta,1).
assertion.objects: The same B,m,A,H,beta,theta; support matrices K,s,lambda and the two actual elliptic curves E_n,E_(n theta), in Kummer coordinates(x+3ell,x-ell).
assertion.hypotheses: B has square reduced denominator,0<B<1/2 and v_p(B)>=4 for p in{2,3,5,7,13}; retain the split-cubic Kummer map, odd local formal-group calculation, local squareclass and reciprocity facts, CRT and Dirichlet.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such B choose m first, then beta,theta; construct one compatible auxiliary-prime assignment for both supports before selecting the actual primes.
assertion.parameter_range: beta>1,theta>=1 are coprime positive squarefree and prime to6; all auxiliary primes are distinct and avoid6 beta theta.
assertion.uniformity: The block determinant argument works for arbitrary d=omega(beta)>=1 and every finite theta support; no finite matrix test substitutes for it.
assertion.constants: The original2730 multiplier catalogue and old-prime valuation4 remain fixed; exactly d-1 I slots plus one q0 slot are used.
assertion.normalizations: Retain actual nonzero beta/theta cross-symbols and their two zero row sums; Ksharp=K+lambda a^t; q0 deletion and full-product determinant coefficient1. Selmer means full2-Selmer, not isogeny Selmer.
assertion.exceptional_cases: d=1 has empty I block; theta=1 permits identical two parameters. Necessary dyadic conditions give only an upper bound; the particular(beta,1) is separately checked locally at every place and independent of rational2-torsion.
assertion.limit_order: Reconcile all Legendre and local conditions before CRT/Dirichlet. Establish exact finite Selmer dimension before full-corank deduction or either use of RC; no rational point or finite Sha inferred here.

assertion.statement: The two actual extra Kummer classes on E_n and E_(n theta), after restricted RC and forward analytic-rank-one imply Sha[2]=0, produce exactly eleven rational witnesses for the original pole template with the same B and m.
assertion.objects: Points(x1,y1),(x2,y2), x_i=A q_i^2, H=theta c^2, e=n/q1^2,z=c q2/q1,r1=y1/q1^3,r2=c^3 y2/(q1^3 z),w=(eHz)^(-1), and the six already chosen bits of m.
assertion.hypotheses: Both n,n theta are positive squarefree congruent11 mod12, with full2-Selmer dimension3, full2-infinity Selmer corank1 and extra class(beta,1) outside all rational2-torsion images. Retain restricted RC, rational modularity and the forward rank-one theorem.
assertion.quantifiers: For the original fixed B,m,A,H and the simultaneous pair n,n theta, choose rational representatives of their actual Kummer classes only after proving Sha[2]=0.
assertion.parameter_range: All q_i,c,e,z are nonzero rational numbers; theta=1 is allowed.
assertion.uniformity: Works for every B in the PC domain supplied by the simultaneous construction; no extra independent multiplier choice.
assertion.constants: Exactly the original six bits and five rational witnesses; no new template variables.
assertion.normalizations: Second point is(Az^2,z r2) on E_(eH). Dividing its cubic equation by z^2 yields r2^2=A(Az^2-eH)(Az^2+3eH), retaining leading factor A.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Extra class excludes infinity and all root points, so ordinates/abscissas and all denominators are nonzero. If theta=1 reuse one point and take q2=q1. Finite Sha is concluded from forward rank only, never assumed for RC.
assertion.limit_order: Exact Selmer dimension then full corank, then two restricted RC applications, then forward rank and Sha[2]=0, then actual points and final rational scaling.

assertion.objects: The classical elliptic j-invariant of E_ell and its quadratic twists, not the quaternionic moduli coordinate also denoted j.

assertion.quantifiers: Every nonzero rational ell and every quadratic twist.

assertion.uniformity: The invariant j is independent of ell; this conclusion does not provide a uniform open-image index.
assertion.constants: c4=208ell^2, discriminant=2304ell^6, j=35152/9;9 does not divide35152.
assertion.normalizations: Use the classical elliptic Weierstrass c4^3/discriminant invariant and the full CM order, including nonmaximal orders.
assertion.exceptional_cases: ell=0 excluded because the curve is singular; no claim about the separate CM generator curve or the quaternionic coordinate.
assertion.limit_order: Compute nonsingular invariants first; use monic integral CM class polynomials to rule out geometric CM before invoking open image.

assertion.objects: Evaluated crossed homomorphisms, the exact kernel of sequences trivial on the full Tate and specified class/quadratic fields, and the fixed scalar z.
assertion.hypotheses: Retain the actual evaluated cocycle identities, fixed scalar acting by u^4 central modulo this kernel, u^4-1 nonzero, and the moving-inertia scalar difference t on the residual test.
assertion.quantifiers: Each permitted characteristic-zero inner test and the outer fraction-field test; residual assertion only for the stated scalar-inertia invariants.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero coefficients where u^4-1 is invertible; residual coefficient field F2((t)) for the separate H0 assertion.
assertion.uniformity: Uses the one fixed scalar already constructed for the fixed elliptic curve; no new field-dependent exponent.
assertion.constants: The same nonzero scalar u^4-1 and residual unit t.
assertion.normalizations: z is central modulo the exact kernel, not itself an element of the kernel. A cocycle vanishing on the kernel satisfies (u^4-1)b(g)=(g-1)b(z).
assertion.exceptional_cases: No residual restriction-injectivity or rank-two localization is claimed; E[2] remains trivial rank2 and residual multiplicity is retained.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the fixed scalar and evaluated cocycle first, restrict to the exact kernel, invert u^4-1 only in characteristic zero; treat residual inertia separately.

connecting_argument: Partitionability gives a nonzero stationary terminal polynomial. Build arbitrarily large cubes based at the unchanged d with unit symbols at all other addresses. Their scalar valuations have one fixed bound after the same denominator clearing. Fix precision above that bound and use a cube dimension larger than the sum of the bounded bit degrees. Use the central corank-zero comparison to obtain the stated normalized L-value bound. The required dimension may depend on d; C1 does not. Empty units use the direct coefficient bound instead.
