assertion.statement: The finite ray-character expansion and arithmetic Frobenius compatibility give the specified centered weight and cancellation O(N log(N)^(-D)) on every interval progression, with W fixed.
assertion.objects: T_C, the ray field K, K intersect Q(zeta_q), mu_C(b), and h_(C,b,W).
assertion.hypotheses: C is conjugation invariant; arithmetic Frobenius is used; W is a fixed multiple of the conductor of K^ab and b is a unit. The separate Hecke and rational prime estimates are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Every fixed D>0 and every interval progression contained in[N].
assertion.parameter_range: All progression steps: large steps use cardinality, small steps use the source estimates.
assertion.uniformity: Uniform in progression and unit b for fixed W; no uniformity as W grows.
assertion.constants: Prime-power L1 error O_H(sqrt(X) log(X)^2); progression error O_(H,W,D)(N log(N)^(-D)).
assertion.normalizations: T_C(p)=2 Lambda_Cprime(p); the character formula has factor1/2 and the denominator [K Q(zeta_q):Q].
assertion.exceptional_cases: Nonunit progression classes contain only primes dividing the modulus; these negligible terms are handled separately.
assertion.limit_order: Fix field, W and source error exponent, then let N grow.

assertion.normalizations: Integer multipliers clear the modular coefficient ambiguities before inversion.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An O(X) translation is retained in weighted coefficient bookkeeping; unbounded affine step is excluded.

assertion.statement: For a bounded finite free complex over a DVR, equality of generic and residue cohomology dimensions in every degree implies free cohomology commuting with reduction; its actual class-functional determinant tensor specializes in the same retained basis.
assertion.objects: A bounded finite free DVR complex C, actual cycle, actual closed functional and retained determinant basis.
assertion.hypotheses: Generic and residue cohomology dimensions agree in every degree. For the stated tensor coordinate the only nonzero dimensions are (1,1) in degrees one and two.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such bounded complex and actual cycle-functional pair.
assertion.parameter_range: A discrete valuation ring A with uniformizer t, fraction field F and residue field k.
assertion.uniformity: An exact algebraic implication; no uniform quantitative bound is inferred.
assertion.constants: No new numeric constant; only unit determinants from contractible summands occur.
assertion.normalizations: Use det inverse C and retain its same contractible-summand identifications before and after reduction.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Dimension equality cannot be omitted. A positive-valuation two-term disk raises residue dimensions in two adjacent degrees and is excluded by the hypothesis.
assertion.limit_order: Smith-reduce the bounded complex; exclude all positive-valuation disks using all-degree dimension equalities; remove only unit disks; specialize the actual tensor.

assertion.statement: At the admitted known simple-zero constituent h with nonzero complementary central value for hk, the generic primitive class-functional coordinate is regular at t=0 and specializes to the actual central tensor.
assertion.objects: The retained primitive complex over Lambda_(t), its actual cycle and closed functional, and the same h,k constituent.
assertion.hypotheses: The first twist has a simple analytic zero and the companion central value is nonzero; forward rank and finiteness, the height formula, nonzero finite-class multipliers, and retained finite free models are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Each admitted known simple-zero constituent satisfying the stated ring-class and local hypotheses.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed K=Q(sqrt(k)), with active primes split in K; localization at (t) with residue Q2.
assertion.uniformity: This proves regularity and tensor identity, not the later numerical valuation bound.
assertion.constants: The generic and central cohomology dimensions are (1,1) in degrees one and two and zero elsewhere.
assertion.normalizations: Cancel only unit disks. The nonzero central cycle gives a nonzero generic kernel; semicontinuity and Euler characteristic then give exact dimension equality.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The unknown base constituent is not assumed to satisfy these analytic hypotheses. No numerical calibration or later uniform determinant bound is used to prove regularity.
assertion.limit_order: Use forward rank and finite Sha at known constituents; establish central dimensions and nonzero cycle; prove generic dimensions; only then apply no-jump specialization.

assertion.statement: At a known simple-zero constituent, the primitive central valuation equals 2j_rc(h,k)-4omega(h)-s(h)-s(hk)-sum_{p|k}t_p+O_{E,pi}(1), with 0<=t_p<=2 and t_p=2 for the full rational two-torsion curve.
assertion.objects: The same retained class-functional tensor, ordinary Kummer complex of Res_{K/Q}(E^h), product E^h times E^(hk), and their dual sum/difference isogenies.
assertion.hypotheses: Known-zero regularity and the same-point central identity, finite Sha from forward theorems, integral Kummer duality, Milne arithmetic isogeny ratio, local quotient lengths and the tame component-group description are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Each admitted h,k with the first twist a known simple zero and companion nonzero central value.
assertion.parameter_range: All active primes split in K; companion primes are tame good primes for E^h. Old local types and L are fixed.
assertion.uniformity: The remaining error depends only on fixed E, pi, old local types and multiplier, not h,k. The companion sum is not absorbed before omega(k) is bounded.
assertion.constants: Ordinary tensor valuation 2j_rc+2v2(Lm)+2g_A-s_A; two moving lengths cancel 2v2(m); each active prime contributes -4; IJ=2, regulator ratio2/I^2, cotangent ab=4.
assertion.normalizations: Use actual integral determinant torsion disks with sign (-1)^(i+1), pullback Neron measures, and the rational points of the finite etale component scheme. No BSD leading-term equality is assumed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not discard degree-one or degree-three rational torsion, absorb unbounded Sha lengths, or replace component schemes by geometric cardinalities. At companion primes the Weil restriction is connected and the ramified twist contributes E[2]^Frob.
assertion.limit_order: Compute ordinary integral torsion and both free coefficients; subtract moving and active quotient lengths; apply the algebraic isogeny ratio with the same measures; retain the negative companion sum until a separate bound permits absorption.

assertion.statement: Each specified actual automorphism of the finite Galois compositum is realized by arithmetic Frobenius at a suitable chosen place over infinitely many rational primes, avoiding the finite exclusions.
assertion.objects: The finite normal composita containing the actual radical, cyclotomic, Tate, ring-class, quadratic and finite cochain data; a single automorphism whose restrictions already agree.
assertion.hypotheses: The extension is finite Galois over Q, the prescribed automorphism exists in its Galois group, and only finitely many primes are excluded.
assertion.quantifiers: For each such finite extension and actual automorphism, infinitely many unramified rational primes and a place over each realizing that representative.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite Galois extensions only; each precision is treated separately.
assertion.uniformity: No effective size bound, infinite-level density or uniformity over extension degree is asserted.
assertion.constants: The nonempty conjugacy class has positive density equal to its size divided by the finite Galois group order.
assertion.normalizations: Arithmetic Frobenius acts by the residue-field norm power. A rational prime determines a conjugacy class; conjugating the place selects the actual representative.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Compatibility on intersections is an input from an actual automorphism, not a consequence of Chebotarev. The theorem does not independently prescribe arbitrary component actions.
assertion.limit_order: Form the finite normal compositum and actual compatible element; apply finite Chebotarev and choose a place; only later pass to the retained precision limit or apply localized model maps.

supplier.statement: For tame totally ramified cyclic degree n with mu_n in the DVR, Edixhoven gives a Néron special-fiber filtration with Gr0=(A′_k)^mu_n and positive graded terms vector groups. Thus F1 is connected and Phi is pi0((A′_k)^mu_n). Proposition4.1 identifies the Weil restriction of the Néron model with the Néron model of the restricted variety; §5.1 identifies its reduction kernel and graded vector-group terms.
